themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Morrisania/Crotona have spiked dramatically THIS WEEK with 33 complaints vs. a 6.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 439% increase (z-score: 8.35)—suggesting widespread pavement, pothole, or surface deterioration that may be accelerating.
evidence: 33 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (439% spike, z-score: 8.35)
Concurrent spike in damaged street signs (5 complaints last week vs. 0.5 avg, 900% increase)
Concurrent spike in air quality complaints (4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 avg, 967% increase, potentially dust/debris from deteriorating streets)
reporting_angles: Walk major streets in Morrisania/Crotona to document potholes, crumbling sidewalks, and debris; geolocate complaints to identify hotspots
Interview DOT about whether there's a recent construction project, weather event, or maintenance backlog causing the sudden deterioration

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Alert
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints in Morrisania/Crotona surged THIS WEEK to 4 complaints vs. a baseline of 0.4 weekly complaints—a 967% spike (z-score: 7.49)—coinciding with street condition and street sweeping spikes, suggesting possible dust, debris, or emissions issues.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Coincides with 33 street condition complaints THIS WEEK (439% spike) and 6 street sweeping complaints 2 weeks ago (1100% spike)
Pattern suggests airborne dust or particles from deteriorating street infrastructure or inadequate sweeping
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and NYC Parks (street sweeping) to determine if there's a service gap or equipment issue
Interview residents about whether they've noticed dust, odors, or breathing difficulties; check for nearby construction or industrial activity

themes_detail.label: Public Order Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Public order complaints in Morrisania/Crotona have spiked sharply: drinking complaints jumped to 13 THIS WEEK (vs. 1.9 weekly average, 593% increase, z-score: 6.07) and encampments spiked 2 weeks ago to 6 complaints (vs. 0.6 average, 860% increase, z-score: 6.27), indicating emerging street-level conditions that may require intervention.
evidence: 13 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (593% spike, z-score: 6.07)
6 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score: 6.27)
Combined signal suggests clustering of homelessness or substance-use issues in specific locations
reporting_angles: Geolocate 311 drinking and encampment complaints to identify specific corridors or parks where problems are concentrated
Interview NYPD, NYC Department of Homeless Services, and local precinct commanders about response strategy and resources

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Morrisania/Crotona spiked 2 weeks ago to 11 complaints vs. a 2.9 weekly average—a 283% increase (z-score: 5.96)—suggesting inadequate sanitation or structural conditions that may be driving pest proliferation.
evidence: 11 rodent complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (283% spike, z-score: 5.96)
Concurrent spike in unsanitary condition complaints (914 total over 90 days, top 4 complaint type) and street sweeping complaints (6 complaints 2 weeks ago, 1100% spike)
Suggests connection between street cleanliness, food availability, and pest population growth
reporting_angles: Request Department of Health complaint records and extermination activity in the district to correlate with 311 spike
Interview residents about whether they've seen increased rat activity, what areas are most affected, and whether trash collection/street sweeping is inadequate

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animals Complaint Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal (kept as pet) complaints spiked 3 weeks ago to 4 complaints vs. a 0.2 weekly baseline—a 1500% increase (z-score: 8.66)—indicating possible enforcement gap or community awareness shift around exotic/dangerous pet ownership.
evidence: 4 illegal animal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Signal is now 3 weeks old (not active this week) but remains statistically extreme
No community board or constituent case data available to triangulate the nature of animals or neighborhoods affected
reporting_angles: Request NYPD Animal Care & Control complaint data and enforcement actions from the past month to understand what species were involved and which streets/blocks
Interview ACC about whether there's a known problem with large or dangerous animals (snakes, pit bulls, etc.) in the district and what enforcement capacity exists
